the: used before a noun to refer to a specific or already-known thing
The cat sat quietly on the windowsill all afternoon.
muscle: a body tissue that contracts to produce movement
Regular exercise helps build muscle and improve endurance.
that: used to identify a specific thing, person, or clause already mentioned
The book that you gave me last year is still on my shelf.
never: at no time; not on any occasion
She had never travelled outside her home country before that trip.
rests: The whole argument rests on a single uncertain assumption.
every: used to refer to each member of a group without exception
Somebody must repaint the roof every few years.
other: different from the one already mentioned; additional
One shoe was blue, and the other was black.
in: expressing location inside or within something
The keys are in the top drawer of the desk.
body: the physical structure of a person or animal
Regular sleep helps the body recover from a long day.
tires: present tense of tire, used with he/she/it; becomes weak from effort
Every other muscle in the body tires.
this: used to refer to a specific thing nearby or just mentioned
This is the best coffee I have had in years.
one: Only one seat was left when we arrived at the theatre.
has: has; present tense of have, third person singular
The library has extended its opening hours during exam season.
to: expressing direction, purpose, or a recipient
The sun has set, the traffic has thinned, and yet the air refuses to cool.
work: activity involving effort, especially to earn a living or achieve something
The difference is not impatience on one side; it is what is doing the work.
for: intended to belong to, or be given to, someone or something
She bought a small gift for her best friend.
eighty: My grandmother just turned eighty last month.
years: Somebody must own the roof and repaint it every few years.
without: not having; in the absence of
This arrangement lets the wheel turn into a lean without anyone touching the handlebars.
stopping: the act of bringing something to an end
Stopping the medicine suddenly can cause side effects.
hold: keep or retain something, such as water or an object
These containers hold enough water for a week.
heavy: The suitcase was too heavy to carry up the stairs alone.
bag: a container made of soft material used to carry things
She packed her bag the night before the trip.
at: used to show a specific place, time or point
We agreed to meet at the station at six o'clock.
arm: the part of the body from the shoulder to the hand
She broke her arm while skiing down the steep slope.
length: how long something is from one end to the other
The length of the bridge is almost two kilometres.
and: used to connect words, phrases, or clauses
We packed sandwiches, fruit, and water for the long hike.
count: say numbers in order to find the total of something
Children learn to count on their fingers before they use written numbers.
seconds: units of time, sixty of which make a minute
The whole process took only a few seconds to complete.
within: inside; before a period of time has passed
Most of a lesson disappears within a single day.
minute: a unit of time equal to sixty seconds
Wait just a minute while I fetch my coat.
begins: The film begins with a dramatic scene in the mountains.
shake: to move quickly and repeatedly from side to side
Her hands began to shake before she stepped on stage.
shortly: The manager will arrive shortly, so please wait in the lobby.
afterwards: The rain stopped, and the sun came out shortly afterwards.
it: used to refer to a thing, animal, or situation already mentioned
She lost her phone and later found it under the sofa.
gives: The charity gives food and shelter to homeless families.
out: away from the inside of a place; not in
She stepped out for a few minutes to get some fresh air.
is: present tense (he/she/it) of the verb be
The library is open until nine o'clock every evening.
normal: usual, typical, or expected; not unusual
It is normal to feel nervous before a big exam.
behaviour: the way a person, animal, or system acts
Scientists studied the herd's behaviour during the sudden storm.
hard: difficult; not easy, or solid to the touch
It was hard to concentrate with all that noise outside.
run: to move quickly, or to continue moving under its own momentum
The car will run for a while even after the engine dies.
short: small in length, distance, or duration
The meeting was surprisingly short this week.
of: used to show belonging, origin, or a relationship between two things
The cover of the book was torn at the corner.
supplies: stocks of things needed, such as food or equipment
Aid workers delivered fresh supplies to the flooded village.
stop: to come to an end or cause something to end
The bus will stop right outside the school gate.
heart: the organ that pumps blood around the body
Exercise strengthens the heart and improves circulation.
not: used to make a statement, verb, or phrase negative
The results are not as clear as we had hoped.
allowed: given permission to happen or be done
được để cho, bị bỏ mặc
Visitors are not allowed to touch the ancient manuscripts in the archive.
option: a thing that may be chosen from a set of possibilities
Renting is often a cheaper option than buying for young families.
part: a piece or portion of a whole
Only a small part of the report dealt with financial risks.
answer: a response given to a question or problem
Her answer to the interview question impressed every member of the panel.
constantly: New apps are constantly being released to compete for users' attention.
just: I just finished reading the report you sent this morning.
very: used to make an adjective or adverb stronger
The soup tasted very good after such a cold walk.
small: not large in size, amount, or degree
They live in a small apartment near the city center.
pieces: portions or parts of something, plural
The vase shattered into pieces when it fell off the shelf.
between: in the space or time separating two things
The old road runs between two small villages in the valley.
beat: a single stroke or pulse, especially of the heart or music
She could feel every beat of her heart after the race.
next: coming immediately after the present one in time or order
We agreed to meet again at the same time next week.
relaxes: The muscle relaxes fully between each contraction of the heart.
completely: The old factory was completely rebuilt after the fire.
resting: relaxing, or in a state of not moving
The cat spent the afternoon resting in the warm sun.
rate: the speed at which something happens, or a fixed price or measure
The company's growth rate slowed considerably during the recession.
recovery: the process of returning to a normal state after illness or difficulty
Doctors were pleased with the patient's fast recovery after the operation.
period: a length or portion of time
The company reported strong growth over the last financial period.
longer: for a greater length of time
Fresh bread stays soft for longer if wrapped properly.
than: used to introduce the second part of a comparison
This year's harvest was larger than last year's.
working: Understanding the pattern is the first step towards working around it.
over: during the whole of a period of time; more than
Prices have risen steadily over the past five years.
day: a period of twenty-four hours, or the time when it is light
She spent the whole day preparing for the interview.
spends: uses time or money on something
She spends most weekends hiking in the mountains.
more: to a greater degree or extent
Careful listeners remember song lyrics more clearly than plain speech.
time: the continuous progress of existence measured in seconds, minutes, hours, etc.
Planting street trees releases water vapour and shades the ground at the same time.
off: not connected, operating, or switched on
Please turn the lights off before you leave the room.
on: positioned at or touching the surface of something
She placed the keys on the table by the door.
rest: the part of something that remains, or a period of relaxation
phần còn lại, sự nghỉ ngơi
After a short rest, they continued walking up the hill.
supply: to provide something that is needed
The factory supplies parts to car makers across the region.
line: a long thin mark or stroke
She drew a straight line across the page with a ruler.
cardiac: The patient was rushed to hospital after a sudden cardiac event.
unusually: in a way that is not common or ordinary
Cardiac muscle is unusually rich in the machinery that turns fuel into work.
rich: having a lot of money or possessions
Only a few rich families could afford imported goods back then.
machinery: machines collectively, or the working parts of a system
Heavy machinery was brought in to clear the collapsed building.
turns: present tense of turn, used with he/she/it; changes direction
When the frame begins to lean to the left, the front wheel turns slightly to the left as well.
fuel: a material burned to produce heat or power
The car ran out of fuel halfway through the trip.
into: moving towards the inside of something
She walked into the room and switched on the light.
fed: given food; past tense of feed
The stray cat was fed by neighbours every evening.
by: indicating the agent, method, or proximity of something
The letter was written by hand and delivered by courier.
its: belonging to a thing, animal, or situation already mentioned
The cat licked its paw before curling up to sleep.
own: to possess something, or belonging to oneself
Few families in the village own a car of their own.
dedicated: used for one particular purpose only
The hospital opened a dedicated ward for children with asthma.
vessels: ships or boats, or tubes carrying blood in the body
Blood flows through tiny vessels to reach every muscle.
also: The recipe also works well with chicken instead of beef.
flexible: able to change or adapt easily
The new policy offers flexible working hours for parents.
about: The lecture was about how cities cope with extreme heat.
what: used to ask for information about something
The reason lies in what cities are actually made of.
burns: consumes fuel to produce energy or heat
This old furnace burns far more oil than a modern one.
switching: changing from one thing, system, or state to another
Switching between the two languages felt natural to her by the end of the trip.
sources: the places or things from which something originates
Journalists must protect the identity of their sources.
according: in a way that agrees with or depends on something
Pay varies according to experience and the hours worked.
available: able to be obtained, used or reached
Tickets for the concert are still available online.
perhaps: used to express uncertainty or possibility; maybe
Perhaps the weather will improve by the time the match begins.
strangest: most unusual or surprising (superlative of strange)
This is the strangest story I have ever heard.
feature: a distinctive or notable part or quality of something
The phone's best feature is its long battery life.
signal: an event or sound that gives a message or triggers an action
The referee's whistle is the signal for the game to begin.
does: performs an action, or auxiliary form used in questions and negatives
She does her best to help everyone around her.
come: to move toward or arrive at a particular place; to originate from
Most of the fruit here comes from small family farms.
from: indicating the point where something starts or originates
The letter came from a friend living overseas.
brain: the organ inside the head that controls thought and body function
Reading regularly keeps the brain active and engaged.
patch: a small area or part of something that differs from its surroundings
A patch of blue sky appeared between the dark clouds.
specialised: designed or trained for a particular purpose or area of expertise
The hospital has specialised equipment for treating burns.
tissue: a group of similar cells forming part of a living organism
A small patch of specialised tissue produces its own rhythm.
produces: The volcano regularly produces small clouds of ash and steam.
rhythm: a regular repeated pattern of movement or sound
The drummer kept a steady rhythm throughout the song.
follows: comes after something in time or order
A short quiz follows each chapter of the textbook.
nerves: fibres that carry signals between the brain and other parts of the body
The dentist numbed the nerves before starting the procedure.
adjust: to change something slightly to make it more suitable
It took her a few weeks to adjust to the new time zone.
speed: the rate at which something moves or happens
The car slowed its speed as it approached the school zone.
but: used to introduce something contrasting with what has just been said
She wanted to stay longer, but the last train was leaving soon.
they: used to refer to people or things already mentioned, as the subject
They arrived late because of heavy traffic on the highway.
are: present tense form of 'to be' used with you, we, they
They are planning to visit their grandparents next weekend.
origin: the point or place where something begins or comes from
The origin of the custom is still debated among historians.
independence: freedom from control or support of others
The country celebrated fifty years of independence this year.
practical: concerned with actual application rather than theory
She gave us some practical tips for managing our time better.
consequence: a result or effect of an action or condition
Losing his job was a direct consequence of the factory closing.
surgeons: Surgeons in the unit rotate shifts to cover emergencies around the clock.
rely: to depend on someone or something with confidence
Many farmers rely on rainfall rather than irrigation systems.
removed: The stubborn stain was finally removed with a strong cleaner.
kept: continued to have, hold, or maintain something
The recipe was kept secret within the family for generations.
supplied: The camp was well supplied with food and clean water.
will: used to express the future tense
A fact heard once looks, from the inside, like a fact that will never be needed again.
go: to move or travel from one place to another
We should go before the traffic gets worse.
beating: the action of a heart pulsing regularly
Doctors could hear the baby's heart beating clearly on the monitor.
while: It makes the city liveable while the wider problem is dealt with separately.
itself: used to refer back to a thing or situation already mentioned, for emphasis
The machine can clean itself without any help from a technician.
need: to require something because it is essential
Plants need sunlight and water in order to grow well.
instructions: detailed information telling someone how to do something
Please read the instructions carefully before assembling the furniture.
needs: The garden needs watering twice a week during summer.
oxygen: a colourless gas that living things need to breathe
Plants release oxygen into the air during photosynthesis.
suitable: right or appropriate for a particular purpose
This film is not suitable for young children.
temperature: a measure of how hot or cold something is
The nurse checked the patient's temperature before the appointment began.
right: correct or suitable for a particular situation
Choosing the right moment to speak up can be difficult.
balance: a state in which different things are of equal weight or importance
Finding a balance between work and rest is not always easy.
salts: crystalline mineral compounds, including but not limited to table salt
The spring water contains several dissolved mineral salts.
price: the amount of money needed to buy something
The price of vegetables usually rises sharply during the winter months.
all: the whole quantity or extent of something
She spent all summer preparing for the entrance exam.
reliability: the quality of being trustworthy and consistently performing well
Customers value the reliability of the brand's washing machines.
narrow: of small width, especially compared with length
Only one car at a time can pass along the narrow bridge.
tolerance: the ability to endure something, or an allowed range of variation
độ dung sai, sự chịu đựng
The price of all this reliability is a narrow tolerance.
skeletal: relating to the bones or skeleton of the body
Skeletal injuries often take much longer to heal than muscle strains.
can: used to express ability or possibility
Anyone with an internet connection can join the online course.
be: to exist, or to have a particular state or quality
It can be difficult to stay calm during an emergency.
starved: severely deprived of something needed, such as food or blood
bị bỏ đói, bị thiếu trầm trọng
The plants looked starved of both water and light.
blood: the red liquid that circulates through the body
The nurse drew a small sample of blood for testing.
many: Many residents still remember the flood of that year.
minutes: units of time equal to sixty seconds
The bus arrived only a few minutes late.
recover: to return to a normal state after illness or difficulty
It took months for the economy to recover after the crisis.
cannot: used to say that something is not possible or not allowed
Visitors cannot enter the site without prior written permission.
cells: plural of cell; the smallest structural units of living organisms
Cancer cells can divide far faster than healthy ones.
lose: to no longer have something; to be deprived of
If you lose your password, you can reset it online.
their: belonging to or associated with the people or things just mentioned
The students left their bags in the classroom overnight.
damaged: harmed or injured in a way that reduces value or usefulness
The damaged bridge remained closed to traffic for several months.
quickly: The fire spread quickly through the dry grass before anyone noticed.
unlike: Tools break, and unlike a damaged book a damaged tool can be dangerous.
most: the majority of; the greatest amount or number of
Most of the guests had already left by the time the rain started.
barely: He barely finished the race before collapsing from exhaustion.
replaced: had something new put in its place
The old traffic lights were replaced with a modern system.
runs: uses up completely, or continues operating
The shop often runs out of fresh bread by midday.
tissues: plural of tissue; groups of cells forming parts of a body
Unlike most tissues, heart muscle will burn whatever fuel is most available.
burn: to consume fuel and produce heat or flame; use as energy
Regular exercise helps the body burn calories more efficiently.
whatever: anything or everything, regardless of what
Some new words were quietly ignored by speakers who preferred whatever they already said.
fats: soft substances found in animal tissue and some foods
A balanced diet includes some healthy fats, such as those in nuts.
sugars: sweet substances, including different types found in food
Fruit contains natural sugars as well as fibre and vitamins.
or: used to link alternatives or possibilities
Would you like tea or coffee with your breakfast?
acids: chemical substances that can react with a base to form a salt
Certain fruit acids can slowly wear away tooth enamel over time.
organs: parts of the body that perform specific functions; plural of organ
Doctors examined several organs to find the source of the infection.
discard: to get rid of something no longer wanted
Please discard any expired medicine safely at the pharmacy.
switches: changes from one thing, system, or state to another
The app switches automatically between light and dark mode at sunset.
them: used to refer to people or things already mentioned, as the object
I called them yesterday but nobody answered the phone.
pausing: stopping briefly before continuing an action
She read the whole report aloud without pausing once.
arranged: planned or organized in advance, or put in a particular order
The books were arranged neatly on the shelf by author.
accordingly: in a way that suits the particular situation; consequently
Prices rose, and the shop adjusted its budget accordingly.
draw: to pull something out, or to create a picture
The magician asked a volunteer to draw a card from the deck.
passing: lasting only a short time; happening while moving by
He gave only a passing glance at the newspaper headlines.
through: moving in one side and out the other; by means of
Brick, asphalt and concrete absorb heat all day and release it slowly through the night.
chambers: enclosed spaces within an organ, especially the heart
The heart has four separate chambers that pump blood around the body.
branching: dividing into separate parts, like a tree's branches
The river keeps branching into smaller streams as it nears the delta.
above: in or to a higher position than something else
A hawk circled slowly above the quiet valley.
exit: a way out of a place, or the act of leaving
The heart's own vessels branch off just above the exit of the chambers.
wrapping: Narrow vessels feed the heart, wrapping around the outside of the muscle.
outside: not inside; in or to a place beyond the boundary of something
The children played outside until it grew dark.
those: used to refer to people or things further away or already mentioned
Those houses on the hill were built a century ago.
fill: to make or become full of something
Please fill the bottle with water before we leave.
mainly: The crowd was mainly made up of young families.
beats: single strokes or pulses, especially of the heart
The doctor counted forty beats in fifteen seconds.
when: The baker's skill lies in knowing when to wait and when to stop waiting.
relaxed: calm and free from tension; loosened
He felt completely relaxed after the long massage.
so: used to show the result or consequence of something
It started raining, so we decided to stay indoors.
driven: operated or pushed forward by force
The factory's machines are driven by a single large motor.
too: The height of the band carries information too.
fast: The train offers a fast way to travel between the two cities.
long: having a great length or duration
It was a long journey across three different countries.
shorten: to make something shorter in length or time
The airline decided to shorten the layover time between connecting flights.
pause: a short stop in an action, speech, or process
There was an awkward pause before anyone answered the question.
which: used to ask about or refer to a specific choice
It is one of the clearest ways in which a city changes its weather.
depends: is affected or determined by something
The success of the picnic depends entirely on the weather.
organ: a part of the body that performs a specific function
The heart is the organ that pumps blood around the body.
hardest: Learning to listen was the hardest part of the course for him.
tire: to become or make weak from effort; to lose energy
So the organ that is hardest to tire is also the one least able to repair itself.
least: Of all the options, this one costs the least money.
able: having the skill, power, or opportunity to do something
She was finally able to finish the marathon this year.
repair: to fix something that is damaged
It took a week to repair the leaking roof.
combination: a joining together of two or more different things
The dish is a combination of sweet and spicy flavours.
explains: makes something clear by describing it in detail
This explains why rereading notes feels productive but works so poorly.
why: Why does the air above a city stay warm long after sunset?
much: to a great extent or degree
The new design does not cost much more than the old one.
medical: relating to the treatment of illness and injuries
She sought medical advice after experiencing chest pains.
attention: notice, thought or interest given to something
The teacher asked the students to pay attention to the diagram.
goes: moves or travels from one place to another
He goes to the gym every morning before work.
keeping: continuing to have, hold, or maintain something
Keeping old letters can help families remember their history.
lines: long thin marks, or routes along which something travels
Workers repaired the telephone lines after the storm.
open: not closed; allowing access, movement, or view
They left the window open to let in the cool evening air.
little: There is little time left before the deadline arrives.
making: Making bread from scratch takes patience and practice.
harder: more difficult or more solid; comparative of hard
The second exam was noticeably harder than the first.
